He thereafter allegedly compelled the complainant to sign certain documents, which the complainant later discovered were bank loan documents on the basis of which the applicant had taken a further loan of Rs. 3,00,000/- on the same vehicle.

It is also stated that the applicant paid eight monthly instalments of Rs.
8,000/- each in respect of the bank loan from 10.12.2022 until 22.09.2023, and that the lender is now threatening to repossess the vehicle.
5.

Ms. Madan submits that the allegations of forgery in the FIR lack credibility, as the allegation against the applicant is that the bank loan documents were signed by the complainant after 30.01.2024, whereas the loan was taken by the applicant from the bank in the year 2022 itself.
It is further submitted that the evidence in the present case is largely documentary, and the applicant is willing to join and cooperate with the investigation.
6. Ms. Dalal, however, submits that the allegations against the applicant are of a serious nature.
The applicant is alleged to have taken the vehicle papers of the complainant in the year 2022 and used them to obtain a loan in his name, which then remained unpaid.
7. Having heard Ms. Madan and Ms. Dalal, I am of the view that this is a fit case for the grant of interim protection at this stage.
The allegations in the FIR pertain to forgery relating to the applicant having taken a bank loan against the complainant's vehicle.
Although the complainant alleges that he was compelled to sign bank loan documents after 30.01.2024, the loan was apparently taken in December 2022 itself.

It appears that the evidence is also largely documentary in nature."
3.
Notice was also issued to the complainant by the aforesaid order.
Although the complainant is not represented today, his presence was recorded in the order dated 25.02.2026.

4. Mr. Aashneet Singh, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, states, upon instructions that the applicant has joined the investigation, and that the dispute between the applicant and the complainant has, in fact, been settled.
5. The status report, alongwith a copy of the Memorandum of Understanding dated 18.02.2026, has been handed up in Court and is taken on record.

sentences.text: Moreover, on 18.02.2026, the complainant also received Rs. 1 Lac cash from alleged Dandona Finance Pvt. Ltd through MoU.
The copy of both MoUs have also attached herewith for the kind perusal of the Hon'ble Court.

In view of the above facts and submissions, it is humbly submitted that the complainant has already received an amount of Rs. 2.5 Lac from the applicant/accused and alleged NBFC."
6.
Ms. Sanigdha Sood Madan, learned counsel for the applicant, also confirms that the disputes between the applicant and the complainant have been settled, and that the amount has been paid.

7. For the aforesaid reasons stated in the order dated 29.01.2026, and in view of the settlement, it is directed that, in the event of arrest in connection with FIR No. 496/2025 dated 04.11.2025,
registered at Police Station Moti Nagar, District West, New Delhi, under Sections 420/468/471 of the IPC, the applicant shall be released on bail, subject to furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 15,000/-, with one surety in the like amount, to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer ["IO"]/Station House Officer ["SHO"], and subject to the following further conditions:
a. The applicant shall appear before the concerned IO as and when required, and cooperate with the investigation.
b. The applicant shall furnish his residential address to the concerned IO/SHO, and shall not change the same without prior intimation to the IO/SHO.
